html:
A Tongan and Fijian writer and anthropologist whose essay "Our Sea of Islands" (1993) changed how many Pacific Islanders see themselves. He argued that the Pacific is not a scatter of tiny, remote islands but a vast connected world of ocean.

Hauʻofa was born in Papua to Tongan missionary parents and studied in Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Canada and Australia. He worked for the king of Tonga and then taught for many years at the University of the South Pacific in Fiji, where he founded the Oceania Centre for Arts and Culture in 1997.

In his essay he answered experts who called island states too small and poor to stand alone. He pointed to the ancestors who sailed across the ocean to trade, marry and make war, as in the Tuʻi Tonga network, and to modern islanders who move and send money between homes across the Pacific Rim. The ocean, he said, joins rather than divides. He also wrote comic fiction about Pacific life, including Tales of the Tikongs and Kisses in the Nederends.
